FILTERS TOUR (2026)
concert - ambient , dream pop

October 10, 2026

this was genuinely some of the most fun i’ve ever had at a concert. it really reminded me why i loved his music so much about a year ago, and it gave me a new understanding and appreciation for the emotional depth and deceptively complex nature of his instrumentation. and his live looping and layering was mesmerizing to see. it’s honestly very impressive how casually he pulled it off.

i met a couple from paraguay waiting for the doors to open. the man was an environmental engineer who was convinced to finally fly to the states because of this concert. they covered my slider as we exchanged song recommendations and recalled our favorite bayonne songs. he told me his favorite was words. and as we all chanted for an encore, and bayonne returned to play that very song, i never felt so connected with a stranger.

they ended up playing four songs from temporary time, which is what i came for, but i left loving his entire discography.

FILTERS (2026)
album - ambient , dream pop

October 10, 2026

it’s definitely a good album, and it’s been growing on me. i really liked the opening with unexpected, and it really set the mood for the album. some of the slickest, pleasing-on-the-ears music i’ve listened to. feels like floating. my other favs are multiphase, january, and recently, forget.

temporary time, his previous album, remains my favorite. but filters shows up with a refreshingly soothing and feel-good vibe that i really dig.

SUSTAINABLE ENERGY: WITHOUT THE HOT AIR (2008)
book - energy , informative

August 20, 2026

really great foundational book on sustainable energy systems, centered around the question of if we can conceivably live on 100% sustainable energy without sacrificing quality of life. mackay has a very straight-to-the-point yet easy to read way of speaking which has influenced the way i write about similar topics. he boiled everything down—from nuclear power plants to the energy required to bike every day—to the same units: kWh per day per person, which made it really interesting to compare, say, how much energy it takes to produce a burger versus flying an international flight. the book summarizes all different sorts of ways of capturing, storing, and using energy, which really puts into perspective how we’ll need a lot of everything to “solve” climate change. as he says:

“If everyone does a little, we’ll only achieve a little.”

as expected, it’s sobering. especially being an american. we emit 24 tons of CO2 a year per person, compared to the 2-3 tons from the “polluted countries” like china and india (not to mention how much manufacturing we outsource to them).

mackay does provide some particularly interesting solutions for the future. he makes a very compelling case that electric cars are a necessity, but also posits the theory that the millions of chargers charging them could adjust their power usage dynamically to make up for the intermittency of renewables. or his idea for congestion-charging, where every car tracks proximity to other vehicles (rather than location, which is controversial), and gets taxed based on that amount.

overall, very solid book that more than anything clarifies and fills in the gaps of the basics of sustainable energy and what the future might look like if we as a species have enough collective self-preservation instinct.

DOPE PURPLE (2026)
concert - psychedelic , noise

June 5, 2026

sooo honestly this show started out feeling like a 2. it was one of my last nights in sweden and i wanted to go out with one of my international friends before i left, so we weren’t going to be picky. it was, by far, the Loudest Band. i had to wear my airpods. and when they say taiwanese psychedelic noise, they mean it. i could barely hear the singer and that man was Screaming.

but i will say, i actually got really into it by the end. it was like a nonstop action scene that somehow started out the gate at the final climax of a movie and ended 5 sequels in at 10 times the budget. they reeled it in in the middle of the set and showed they had dynamics. but yeah i can’t say i’ve ever felt like moving at 100mph standing in one spot before.

OBSESSION (2026)
movie - horror

June 1, 2026

yes, i know this is a really popular movie to like. but i was genuinely really surprised by this, since i had zero expectations and had never heard of curry before this. not only did it have one of the thickest, creepiest atmospheres i’ve seen, it GENUINELY had an substantial message. a lot of horror nowadays (i can’t comment on older horror) just seems like a collection of scary concepts rather than a unified story.

obsession was different. every scene (almost) had a purpose and the characters were genuinely relatable despite being in horror-land. the horror itself was rooted in real emotions and situations that people experience: toxic relationship dynamics, loneliness insecurities, the “nice guy” coverup. it’s a type of horror that for once extends beyond the screen and makes you think about your own life and relationships.

now maybe i’m rating this so high because there’s a relatively low bar in horror movies (to my knowledge, i would love to be proven wrong). not everything made sense, like i still don’t get why nikki fed bear his cat. nikki could’ve had a smoother transition into going insane or there could’ve been a more relatable exploration of why bear’s control over her is a Bad Thing without it being because she’s going rabid. but after all, it’s a horror movie. and for what it’s worth, it packed a ton of really creepy scenes into one film and tied them up about as good as you can.

and god that bedroom corner scene was quite possibly the best horror sequence EVER. curry barker deserves it all.

January

IRON LUNG (2026)
movie -

January 31, 2026

MAJOR inspiration for me right here in multiple respects.

iron lung itself (the game) was a really big source of inspiration for my gamedev journey a few years back. the fact that such a simple game, with a simple premise, was so successful because of good worldbuilding and atmosphere made david szymanski basically a role model for me.

and the fact that it was turned into a movie, by essentially an indie filmmaker (ignoring the whole youtuber part), and i was WATCHING IT IN SWEDEN (it was supposed to be US only), blew my mind. it single-handedly triggered my continuation of development on tracerouter. i remember the very next day, deciding that i would make a new release, and opening up the project for the first time in months.

the movie itself was awesome. i totally get why some people feel like it dragged on, for the same reason people felt like backrooms dragged on. the filmmakers believe in the atmosphere and commit to it; it’s what the original game did. it’s like an electronic trance song: the repetition gives you the space to sink into the layers and become something else entirely. yes, it wouldn’t be the easiest rewatch. but going in for the first time, it felt like a great pace.

i also get why people felt like there wasn’t enough explanation of the lore. i even felt a pang of that. but i understand why it wouldn’t fit into the movie. and i also get why people didn’t like it because of the acting. mark isn’t a professional actor and he happens to be basically the only one on screen for 2 hours.

i think the review by hbomberguy on letterboxd that Mark read out sums it up better than i ever could.
